State Employee

Employee

In the state's central payroll system, an Employee is any individual who provides service for compensation who is hired, elected or appointed to a position within state government. An employee and an FTE (full-time equivalent) are not the same thing. An employee is a person, while an FTE is equivalent to a certain number of hours worked or authorized to be worked.

Position

Positions are defined by SDCL 3-6A-2 as "a collection of duties and responsibilities assigned by the appointing authority." Positions are neither appropriated nor restricted in number by the legislature, but instead are a tool used to manage the workforce. A position is not the same as an employee or an FTE.
Last NameFirst NameMIAgencyTitleSalary/WagePay Basis

Pay Basis

State employee pay is typically paid either on an hourly or annual basis. An hourly employee will get their hourly wage for each hour worked, while a salaried employee will get 1/24th of their annual salary each pay period. The salary of each member of the Legislature is equal to one-fifth of the South Dakota median household income reported by the United States Census Current Population Survey and an additional per diem while in session for room and board. The salary is converted to a daily rate for purposes of paying legislators during session. For non-session meetings, legislators get a flat daily rate; as do members of boards and commissions.
